strengths: Does not clone the trash-can sibling: 1995/bin history stays out; this piece is tabearuki manners and sidewalk logistics.
Stall-as-purchase versus wicket-bento, and tachi-gui versus walking, are angles generic “don’t eat while walking in Japan” posts usually skip.
Closing refuses national-personality proof and treats the habit as a workable response to crowding, wrapping, and disposal.
Visitor tips include “do not scold” and umbrella-plus-food—specific, not a purity lecture.

issues.problem: Festival / ice cream / Harajuku is the same exception set many manners blogs already list; originality lives in the stall/wicket and pause-as-logistics framing, which can get buried under the list.
issues.suggestion: If trimming, cut duplicate scenario beats rather than the local distinctions.
